goal: Improve Qwen3.8-27B on blackbox web-security tasks using only Fleet cyber training tasks.
scope: The rankings are informed starting points, not measured results. Each comparison should change only the settings named by its shaded cells. The fixed 17-task Fleet development set is used to choose settings. The 8-task final Fleet set stays untouched until finalists are chosen. WebExploitBench is run immediately after every accepted checkpoint as a report-only transfer check, but it is never used to choose training settings, checkpoints, or finalists.

groups.label: Run order
columns: The recommended order. Operational checks must pass before longer RL runs.
A stable short name for the exact run or current cluster job.
The single main question this run is designed to answer.
Whether the run failed cleanly, is queued, planned, or waiting on evidence.
Why this run belongs here instead of earlier or later.
The run or starting model that makes this result interpretable.
The evidence required before this run may use GPUs.

groups.label: Model and training system
columns: The model family and size being updated.
The exact model weights used before RL begins.
The immutable version of the starting model files.
The named software that generates attempts, computes rewards, and updates the model. SkyRL and Miles/FTI are two different implementations.
The update method. GRPO compares several attempts on the same task and reinforces actions from attempts that score above their group average.
Whether all weights or only adapters are updated.
The numerical format used for weights and calculations.
The fixed model used to measure how far the policy moves.

groups.label: Tasks and sampling
columns: Which balanced assignment puts tasks into training, development, and final groups.
Tasks used to collect fresh scored attempts for updates.
Unseen tasks used to compare settings; never used for updates.
Unseen tasks held back until finalists are chosen.
How training tasks are chosen for each update.
Whether tasks are mixed or ordered by difficulty.
Distinct tasks contributing scored groups to one update.
Whether attempts from earlier updates are used again.
The fixed number controlling repeatable task sampling.

groups.label: Agent and limits
columns: The program around Qwen that manages messages and tools.
How messages and tool results become Qwen tokens.
The tools available during a training attempt.
How the agent continues near its token limit.
The maximum tokens in the active conversation.
The maximum new model tokens in one attempt.
The maximum new model tokens in one response.
The largest number of model responses in one attempt.
Wall-clock time allowed for a complete attempt.
Wall-clock time allowed for one tool call.
Maximum characters returned by one tool call.
Whether multiple tool calls may run together.
The bounded rule for excluding and replacing a technically broken attempt. A broken attempt is never scored as a model failure.

groups.label: Attempt generation
columns: Independent attempts compared on one task.
Task groups generated for one update.
Total fresh scored attempts used for one update.
Randomness used while sampling training attempts.
Cumulative token probability kept during sampling.
Maximum next-token choices kept; disabled means no fixed count.
The exact integer used for attempt randomness.

groups.label: Reward
columns: The task's real hidden checker that supplies the score.
How the official score becomes a number for RL.
Whether verified intermediate progress contributes reward.
Extra reward for written analysis beyond the official score.
How a technically invalid attempt is preserved and kept out of reward and training.
How a genuine model attempt at the fixed limit is distinguished from a technical timeout.
What happens when every attempt in a group gets the same reward.
How scores are centered and scaled before updating.
Whether unusually high or low rewards are capped.
When a score becomes available to the optimizer.

groups.label: Policy update
columns: Optimizer passes over one new attempt batch.
The size of each model update.
The rule that turns RL gradients into weight updates.
How an attempt's reward is compared with peer attempts.
Penalty strength for moving away from the starting model.
Whether the stay-close reference changes during a long run.
How far a worse action's probability may fall in one update.
How far a better action's probability may rise in one update.
Whether long and short responses receive equal total weight.
An added loss term that rewards a broader action distribution.
Total attempts contributing to one update.
Responses processed at once on each GPU.
How often generators receive updated weights.
The early fraction over which actor learning rate rises.
A penalty that gently pulls weights smaller.
The exact integer controlling repeatable training randomness. The current native launchers use the same integer for training and generation.

groups.label: Computing, tracking, and evaluation
columns: The number of eight-GPU computers used.
The GPUs used on each computer.
Model servers producing training attempts per node.
GPUs cooperating to serve one Qwen copy.
Whether generation and updating share GPUs.
The queue class; c1 is the highest authorized for this project.
How often unseen Fleet development tasks run.
How often recoverable state is saved.
What is sent to Weights & Biases; private prompts and traces are excluded.
Whether a checkpoint reloads without another update.
Unseen Fleet tasks used to choose settings.
Independent attempts on each development task.
When untouched final Fleet tasks may be used.
When the public benchmark runs and how it is treated.
Frozen programs around the model in external evaluation.
How one saved checkpoint is chosen.
Evidence that ends a run early.
Evidence required before a larger run.
The exact integer used by the fixed Fleet development attempts.
Rough cost versus the one-update four-node Miles gate.

defaults.backend: Fleet Miles/FTI RL system with the qualified OpenCode adapter for Fleet tasks
defaults.algorithm: GRPO through Miles: compare attempts within each task group
defaults.harness: OpenCode 1.18.27 through the qualified Miles adapter
defaults.tools: The exact OpenCode challenge-shell and report-submission tool interface
defaults.compaction: Audited OpenCode compaction that preserves task and tool state
defaults.response_tokens: No small cumulative cap; bounded by turns, time, and verified compaction
defaults.invalid_retry: Preserve and exclude the invalid attempt; allow at most one predeclared replacement for its slot; abort the update if the full valid group is still incomplete
defaults.invalid_handling: Exclude from rewards and optimizer input; keep a visible invalid counter; never convert a technical failure into zero reward
defaults.timeout_handling: A healthy attempt that reaches the fixed model time limit receives its official score; a technical timeout is excluded as invalid
defaults.zero_variance_groups: Keep and record; no update signal
defaults.reward_delay: After the complete task group finishes
defaults.inference_engines: Miles distributed generation workers under the exact qualified contract
defaults.tensor_parallel: 8 GPUs per model copy; context parallel size 4
defaults.placement: Exact qualified 4-node, 32-GPU Miles placement; no inferred alternative
defaults.wandb: Loss, reward, lengths, invalids, updates, and GPU use; no prompts or traces
defaults.webexploitbench: Immediately after every accepted checkpoint; report-only transfer check, never a selection signal
defaults.checkpoint_choice: Highest Fleet development-task score; earlier checkpoint wins a tie
defaults.stop_rule: Non-finite values, no valid rewards, broken checkpoint, or confirmed stall
defaults.advance_rule: Real reward, nonzero update, reload, clean release, and Fleet dev lift

changes.backend: Fleet's native SkyRL training path with its separately qualified OpenCode task adapter
changes.algorithm: Native SkyRL GRPO with one optimizer pass, stay-close penalty 0.001, and no automatic replacement sampling

changes.replay: None; resume mode is disabled and each task group is generated fresh

changes.compaction: No compaction in this SkyRL path; reject the whole batch if an attempt reaches a context, generated-token, or turn limit

changes.tool_seconds: 330 seconds, bound in the frozen SkyRL data manifest
changes.tool_output_chars: 50,000 characters, bound in the frozen SkyRL data manifest
changes.parallel_tools: No; the qualified SkyRL parser accepts one tool call per turn
changes.invalid_retry: No replacement in the native SkyRL path; preserve the invalid attempt, clean up every sibling environment, and abort the whole batch
changes.temperature: 1.0 for training generation; 0.0 for development evaluation
changes.official_grader: Exact Fleet hidden checker through the shared single-attempt episode code
changes.invalid_handling: Exclude the invalid attempt from reward and training, then abort the whole batch after every environment is cleaned up; never turn a technical failure into zero reward

changes.weight_refresh: After every optimizer update through the colocated native SkyRL engines

changes.placement: SkyRL places generation, the updated model, and the fixed reference model together on the same 8 GPUs
changes.scheduler: Constant learning rate with zero warmup, as rendered by training/skyrl.py
changes.fleet_dev: 17 development tasks before training and after the final update
changes.wandb: Native SkyRL loss, reward, attempt length, update, and GPU measures; no prompts or traces
changes.recovery_test: Reload the exact native SkyRL checkpoint before any longer successor
changes.webexploitbench: Immediately after every accepted checkpoint; report-only transfer check, never a selection signal
changes.checkpoint_choice: Highest Fleet development-task score; the earlier checkpoint wins a tie
changes.stop_rule: Any invalid batch, non-finite value, missing valid reward variation, broken checkpoint, or confirmed stall
changes.advance_rule: At least one valid task group has real reward variation, one finite nonzero optimizer update completes, the checkpoint reloads, and every owned GPU is cleanly released; Fleet development lift is not required for this operational gate
